Batch 98 Forensic Discoveries

Batch 98 recovers and dates 12 exceptional archival recordings spanning comedy film music and touring history, legendary sports broadcasting, top-40 music radio culture, patriotic choral orchestrations, and wartime military drama: 3 iconic Laurel and Hardy rarities including their film song 'Lazy Moon' from Pardon Us (1931), Marvin Hatley's original arrangement of 'The Dance of the Cuckoos' (1932), and Stan Laurel & Oliver Hardy's heartfelt personal radio broadcast to fans during their 1947 British music hall tour, Hall of Fame pitcher Bob Feller recounting Red Grange's historic 1925 NFL pro debut and Ernie Calverley's legendary 60-foot buzzer-beater in the 1946 NIT (1971), 2 vintage 1968 airchecks from radio king Cousin Brucie (Bruce Morrow) on 77 WABC New York, Fred Waring and The Pennsylvanians performing wartime choral arrangements for the Armed Forces Radio Service (1943), William Bendix starring in The Marine Story (1953), Fanny Brice performing Baby Snooks on Treasury Star Parade (1942), and United Nations Radio's global technical assistance documentary (1952).
